paragraphs: On Monday, Leo read an email from his pen pal, Ravi. Ravi lived in Singapore, and Leo had not met him. Ravi sent a photo of a long paper plane with big wings. "Can you make one?" Ravi wrote. "Please keep in contact, and send me a photo of your plane." Leo was a beginner, but he wanted to try. He drew a plane in his notebook.

On Thursday, the Explorers met in the school library. Teacher Kim gave Leo various kinds of paper. There was white paper, gray paper from an old newspaper, and thin blue paper. First, Leo folded the white paper. His plane had short, flat wings. He threw it, but it fell on the floor. "It does not fly straight," said Leo.

"Look at this book," said Mia. "A bird has long wings, and it can fly very far." Mia loved birds, so she knew many facts about them. Leo looked at the picture for a long time. Then he folded a new plane, and this time the wings were long. "I am the pilot, and I am ready," said Leo. He threw the plane, and it flew across the library. The other children clapped, and Leo smiled.

After that, Teacher Kim took an electric fan from the cupboard. "Let's test the planes with some wind," she said. She put the fan at one end of the long table. Everybody came to watch. Leo tested the white plane first, and the wind pushed it to the side. Then he tested the plane from newspaper paper. It was heavier, so it flew straight against the wind. "Now I know how to improve my planes," said Leo.

Finally, Lily took a photo of Leo with his best plane. That evening, Leo sent the photo to Ravi. "My plane has long wings, and it flies straight," he wrote. Leo was very happy with his plane. Ravi wrote back, "That is a great plane, Leo!" "Next time, let's make a plane together online," Ravi wrote. Leo smiled, because he was not a beginner now.
